Green Bay's defense knocked Chicago starting quarterback Jay Cutler out of the game and intercepted three passes, one of which was returned for a score, and another which ended a last-minute drive for a potential tying touchdown. With this win, the Packers became the first NFC #6 seed to advance to the Super Bowl by defeating the top three seeded teams on the road.
Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers opened up the game with two completions to Greg Jennings for gains of 26 and 22 yards. A few plays later, he threw a 22-yard completion to Jordy Nelson at the Bears 2-yard line, setting up his 1-yard touchdown run to give the Packers an early 7–0 lead. Later on, Tim Masthay's 32-yard punt pinned Chicago back on their 2-yard line. The Bears were unable to move the ball, and Tramon Williams returned Brad Maynard's punt six yards to the 44. Rodgers then completed passes to Brandon Jackson and Nelson for gains of 16 and 15 yards on the way to a 4-yard touchdown run by James Starks.
With time running out in the half, Rodgers threw a pass that was intercepted by Lance Briggs and returned to the Chicago 43. But Cutler returned the favor with an interception thrown to Sam Shields and the score remained 14–0 going into halftime. Cutler was injured on the play and although he returned for a few plays in the third quarter, he ended up having to sit the rest of the second half out.
After forcing Chicago to punt on the opening second-half drive, Green Bay drove to the Bears 6-yard line. But linebacker Brian Urlacher ended the drive by intercepting Rodgers and returning the ball 39 yards before Rodgers made a touchdown-saving tackle on the 45. However, Chicago could not take advantage of the turnover and had to punt. Cutler's replacement, Todd Collins, ended up being ineffective, throwing four consecutive incompletions before being benched in favor of Caleb Hanie with less than a minute left in the third quarter.
Early in the fourth quarter, Hanie's 32-yard completion to Johnny Knox moved the ball to the Packers 1-yard line, setting up a touchdown run by Chester Taylor that cut the score to 14–7. But three drives later, Hanie threw a short pass over the middle that was intercepted by nose tackle B. J. Raji and returned 18 yards for a touchdown. Hanie responded with four consecutive completions on the Bears' next drive and finished it with a 35-yard touchdown throw to Earl Bennett, making the score 21–14. Then after forcing a punt, Chicago got the ball back with 2:53 remaining in the game and managed to drive to the Packers' 29-yard line. But Green Bay's defense managed to hang on for the win, ending the drive with Shields' second interception with 37 seconds left in regulation.
Jennings caught eight passes for 130 yards. Bears running back Matt Forte rushed for 70 yards and caught 10 passes for 90. Shields had four tackles, two interceptions, a sack, and a forced fumble. Urlacher had nine tackles, a sack, and an interception. At 338 pounds, Raji became the heaviest player in NFL history to score a touchdown.
In possibly the NFL's first player-on-player social media attack, Cutler was being criticized for not returning within seconds after leaving the game instead of waiting for explanations in postgame media sessions.[5][6][7] Bears coach Lovie Smith later stated that the choice was not Cutler's decision.[8] Smith made the decision to bench Cutler after consulting the medical and training staff.[9] An MRI revealed the following day that he had sprained his MCL.[10]
The Bears would not return to the playoffs again until 2018.
This was the second postseason meeting in the history of the Bears-Packers rivalry, with Chicago having won the prior meeting 33–14 in the 1941 Western Division playoff.

Pittsburgh jumped to an early 24–0 lead and held off a desperate comeback rally to earn their third Super Bowl bid in the last six years.
Steelers running back Rashard Mendenhall rushed eight times for 28 yards on their opening drive, which took over nine minutes off the clock and ended with his 1-yard touchdown run. Then he rushed four times for 22 yards and caught an 18-yard pass on a drive to the Jets' 32-yard line. Linebacker Bryan Thomas ended the drive with an interception, but the Steelers forced a punt and drove for another score, aided by Mendenhall's 35-yard burst. Shaun Suisham finished the drive with a 20-yard field goal to make the score 10–0. Following another punt, Ben Roethlisberger completed a 24-yard pass to tight end Heath Miller, a 20-yarder to Emmanuel Sanders, and a 14-yard throw to Mendenhall on the way to a 2-yard touchdown run. Two plays after the ensuing kickoff, Ike Taylor sacked Jets quarterback Mark Sanchez on a defensive back blitz and forced a fumble, which cornerback William Gay returned 19 yards for a touchdown, increasing their lead to 24–0 with just over a minute left in the half. This time New York managed to respond, with Sanchez completing four passes for 39 yards on a drive that ended with a 42-yard field goal by Nick Folk, cutting the score to 24–3 going into halftime.
New York took the second-half kickoff and scored with just five plays. Shonn Greene started the drive with a 23-yard run, while Sanchez finished it with a pair of completions to Santonio Holmes, the first for 16 yards, and the second a 45-yard touchdown completion. Pittsburgh responded with a drive to the Jets' 37-yard line but turned the ball over when safety Brodney Pool intercepted a pass from Roethlisberger inside the 10. After an exchange of punts, the Jets converted two fourth downs on a 17-play drive to a first down on the Steelers' 2-yard line. But Pittsburgh's defense made a key goal-line stand. First Greene tried to run up the middle but was stuffed at the 1-yard line. Then Sanchez threw an incomplete pass and another that was batted down by linebacker LaMarr Woodley. On fourth down, LaDainian Tomlinson tried to run through the middle, but Brett Keisel and Casey Hampton tackled him for no gain, turning the ball over.
On the next play, Roethlisberger fumbled a snap and was downed in the end zone for a safety. New York then drove 58 yards following the free kick and scored with Sanchez's 4-yard touchdown pass to Jerricho Cotchery, cutting their deficit to 24–19 with 3:06 left in the game. But the Steelers managed to pick up two key first downs on their next drive with a 14-yard reception by Miller and a 14-yard catch by Antonio Brown on third down and six with less than two minutes left, enabling them to run out the rest of the clock.
Mendenhall rushed for 121 yards and a touchdown, while also catching two passes for 32. Sanchez threw for 233 yards and two touchdowns. Pool had six tackles and an interception.
As of 2025, this is the Jets' most recent playoff game, and the latest AFC Championship Game to not feature either the New England Patriots or the Kansas City Chiefs.[11]
This was the second postseason meeting between the Jets and Steelers, with Pittsburgh winning the only prior meeting 20–17 in overtime in the 2004 AFC Divisional playoffs.

Jay Cutler Gets Ripped by NFL Players, Past and Present, on Twitter
===================================================================

![Image 1](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=129&d=identicon&r=g)by[](https://nesn.com/author/)

Jan 24, 2011

*   [](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Jay%20Cutler%20Gets%20Ripped%20by%20NFL%20Players%2C%20Past%20and%20Present%2C%20on%20Twitter&url=https%3A%2F%2Fnesn.com%2F2011%2F01%2Fjay-cutler-gets-ripped-by-nfl-players-past-and-present-on-twitter%2F)
*   [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnesn.com%2F2011%2F01%2Fjay-cutler-gets-ripped-by-nfl-players-past-and-present-on-twitter%2F)

[![Image 2: Jay Cutler Gets Ripped by NFL Players, Past and Present, on Twitter](https://s47719.pcdn.co/wp-content/uploads/2012/08/6a0115709f071f970b0147e1e9d1dc970b.jpe)](http://nesn.com/2011/01/jay-cutler-gets-ripped-by-nfl-players-past-and-present-on-twitter.html) The world of Twitter has been set ablaze by NFL players, this time ripping **Jay Cutler** to shreds following and during the 21-14 loss the Bears suffered on Sunday in Chicago.

The tweets, flying in from across the league as players watched from home, questioned both the legitimacy of the injury as well as Cutler’s heart and intensity. Upon hearing the news, [he allegedly started crying by his locker](http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2011/01/24/jay-cutler-had-tears-in-his-eyes-when-told-other-players-ripped-him/).

Cutler appeared to tweak his knee during the first half of the NFC Championship game and was pulled during the third quarter. He was spotted standing on the sidelines, riding the exercise bike and pouting on the bench for the rest of the game, which didn’t sit well with many former and current players.

Jacksonville Jaguars star running back **Maurice Jones-Drew** [tweeted](http://twitter.com/Jones_Drew32): "Hey I think the **Urban Meyer** rule is in effect right now…when the going gets tough… QUIT" and added "All I’m saying is that he can finish the game on a hurt knee…I played the whole season on one."

Eagles cornerback **Asante Samuel** also joined in on the Cutler bashing, [tweeting](http://twitter.com/Thepresidentcb): "If he was on my team I’d be looking at him sideways."

Cardinals defensive end **Darnell Dockett** [added](http://twitter.com/ddockett): "If I’m on Chicago team Jay Cutler has to wait till me and the team shower get dressed and leave before he comes in the locker room!"

Former great **Deion Sanders** chimed in too, writing, "Folks i never question a players injury but i do question a players heart."

Redskins wide receiver **Anthony Armstrong** had the tweet of the day, [tweeting](http://twitter.com/ddockett): "Knee-Gate in Chicago."

During the postgame news conference, Cutler’s teammates and coaches were supportive of Cutler and defensive about the circumstances surrounding the injury. Linebacker **Brian Urlacher** called him "tough as hell" while coach **Lovie Smith** reiterated that he was simply injured and that was the end of the story.

Cutler is set to undergo an MRI Monday, and pending the results, some players might have to backpedal on these strong statements.

One of the defining moments for Jay Cutler as a professional football player came in January of 2011. He’d just led the Chicago Bears in a playoff victory over the Seattle Seahawks. A game where he accounted for four touchdowns. Arguably the best overall performance of his career. Now he’d have a chance to slay some demons in the NFC championship against the Green Bay Packers. Sadly, most people know the story.

At some point in the first half, Cutler suffered a slight tear to his MCL that took away the use of his knee. He was a sitting duck out there, unable to run or plant his leg to throw. So the decision was made to bench him in favor of backup Todd Collins in the second half. That soon became a switch to Caleb Hanie after a couple of series. Yet all people could talk about was Cutler sitting on the sideline, stonefaced watching the game.

This led to rampant social media rants from fans and players alike calling the quarterback out for not being tough enough. A stigma he would carry for the rest of his career. When asked about that during his appearance on the Pardon My Take [podcast](https://www.stitcher.com/podcast/pardon-my-take/e/66934955?autoplay=true), Cutler admitted that it still bothers him to this day.

> “I mean I’ve been through some crazy stuff. Concussions. Broken stuff. It just is what it is. So I think for me to have that part questioned? That hurt. That was tough. That was a tough one to swallow. To say I wasn’t good or anything else, I’m fine with that. There may be some truth to that. But to say I just didn’t want to play anymore?”

### **Jay Cutler describes the chaos of what happened**

The truth is Cutler tried to gut it out. He wanted to play. However, it only took one pass attempt in the second half for him to realize that he was next to useless out there. So he made the tough decision to sit, putting his fate in the hands of somebody else. That obviously wasn’t easy. One thing he does admit made matters worse though was him staying on the sideline for the second half.

Subscribe to the [BFR Youtube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCyLW3yO6FXCBQRdu5G5VbQg) and ride shotgun with Dave and Ficky as they break down Bears football like nobody else.

> “It was right before halftime. We went in, taped it up, then I came out and I think I literally threw one ball and my knee just buckled. It went straight in the ground. Then I said like, ‘I don’t think I can throw and I don’t think I can run.’…And that’s where it gets tricky. Do I just stay on the sideline? I think now they take you in (to the locker room). You can’t just leave them sitting out there.”

It’s really unfair for Cutler to shoulder that much blame. He didn’t get a lot of help from his offensive line that day. It was just a case of bad luck made worse by a team that wasn’t prepared for how drastic an impact social media would have on the situation. Nobody should ever question his toughness. It wasn’t about pain in this situation. It was the functionality of a body part crucial to his position.

Jay Cutler Sprained MCL In Knee
===============================

January 24, 2011 / 10:23 AM CST / CBS Chicago

[Add CBS News on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbsnews.com)

_UPDATED: 1/24/2011, 3:10 p.m._

**CHICAGO (CBS)** \-- Chicago Bears' quarterback Jay Cutler sprained a knee ligament in the NFC Championship game against the Green Bay Packers, Bears Coach Lovie Smith confirmed Monday.

Sean Jensen, of the Chicago Sun-Times, first reported on [his Twitter account](http://twitter.com/skjensen) that Cutler tore the medial collateral ligament (MCL) on his left knee. Jensen later confirmed that Cutler suffered a Grade II sprain of his MCL, an injury that typically takes 3-4 weeks to heal.

Smith said that Cutler suffered a sprain to his MCL. A sprain usually means that the ligament was torn slightly, but not severely. He said that if the Bears made the Super Bowl, Cutler's status would have been questionable.

Smith also took aim at critics who questioned Cutler's toughness or ability to play in the game. Smith said it was the decision of the coaches and training staff to pull the quarterback from the biggest game of his career so far.

"If you're going to attack somebody, you should be attacking me as the head football coach," Smith said. "He wanted to go back in."

Depending on the severity of the tear, it takes up to six weeks for a MCL injury to heal--often less. The initial treatment focuses on reducing the pain and inflammation in the knee.

Typically, the injury is treated with ice, anti-inflammatory medication and stabilizing the joint with a brace. In most cases, surgery is not needed and prospects for a complete recovery are excellent.

During the second half of the game, the Internet and Twitter were abuzz with current and former NFL players having knee-jerk reactions to Cutler's injury. Linebacker Brian Urlacher and Coach Lovie Smith quickly came to Cutler's defense.

"Jay was hurt. I don't question his toughness, he's tough as hell," Urlacher said. "He's one of the toughest players on our football team. He doesn't complain when he gets hit. He goes out there and plays every Sunday, he practices every single day, so no we don't question his toughness."

There were more than a few comments on Twitter when it became clear Cutler would not be back.

"If I'm on chicago team jay cutler has to wait till me and the team shower get dressed and leave before he comes in the locker room!" Arizona Cardinals defensive lineman Darnell Dockett tweeted.

"Folks i never question a players injury but i do question a players heart," wrote Deion Sanders, former cornerback and current NFL analyst.

According to locker room reports, Cutler became emotional, with tears welling up in his eyes, when he was told of the criticism.

Bears coach Lovie Smith grew testy after being asked about Cutler's injury.

"He hurt his knee and he was out, all right?" Smith said. "There's nothing else for me to tell you on that. I don't know exactly when it happened, he couldn't go and that was that."

Added Urlacher: "Nothing like jealous people at home watching. Players around the league you said, right? Yeah, I love jealous people when they are watching our game on TV while their season is over."

Crucial B.J. Raji Interception Result of Perfectly Timed Zone Blitz in Packers’ NFC Championship Win
====================================================================================================

![Image 1](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=129&d=identicon&r=g)by[](https://nesn.com/author/)

Jan 23, 2011

*   [](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Crucial%20B.J.%20Raji%20Interception%20Result%20of%20Perfectly%20Timed%20Zone%20Blitz%20in%20Packers%26%238217%3B%20NFC%20Championship%20Win&url=https%3A%2F%2Fnesn.com%2F2011%2F01%2Fcrucial-bj-raji-interception-result-of-perfectly-timed-zone-blitz-in-packers-nfc-championship-win%2F)
*   [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnesn.com%2F2011%2F01%2Fcrucial-bj-raji-interception-result-of-perfectly-timed-zone-blitz-in-packers-nfc-championship-win%2F)

[![Image 2: Crucial B.J. Raji Interception Result of Perfectly Timed Zone Blitz in Packers' NFC Championship Win](https://s47719.pcdn.co/wp-content/uploads/2012/08/6a0115709f071f970b0147e1e43a2a970b.jpe)](http://nesn.com/2011/01/crucial-bj-raji-interception-result-of-perfectly-timed-zone-blitz-in-packers-nfc-championship-win.html) The timing was brilliant. As Bears third-string quarterback **Caleb Hanie** was developing a rhythm and finding some real comfort in the pocket, Packers defensive coordinator **Dom Capers** dialed up an old-school favorite, calling for a zone blitz that confused Hanie and changed the pulse of Sunday’s NFC Championship.

Packers nose tackle **B.J. Raji**, a 337-pound Boston College alum, dropped into coverage, hauled in Hanie’s throw and returned the interception 18 years for a touchdown that gave the Packers a two-score lead in an eventual 21-14 victory.

The zone blitz can kill a young quarterback, and Hanie — who entered the game as the proud owner of 66 career passing yards — had no chance. It was the decisive play of Green Bay’s terrific defensive performance that rescued quarterback **Aaron Rodgers** from a rough day. The MVP candidate was excellent in the Packers’ two previous playoff games and led a nice touchdown drive to open the game, but he finished 17-for-30 for 244 yards, two interceptions and one rushing score.

The Packers’ defense, which was ranked fifth in yardage and second in scoring in the regular season, didn’t slump at all. They had three interceptions, two sacks and held Chicago to 50 percent passing and 1 of 13 on third down. They also had six quarterback hits, four tackles for loss and one forced fumble.

To be fair, the Bears at times tried to make it easy on the Packers. Starting quarterback **Jay Cutler** had a poor effort and left the game with an apparent knee injury in the third quarter, and backup **Todd Collins** — the only quarterback in the NFL this season with two games with a passer rating of less than 10 — didn’t complete a pass in two drives.

That left Hanie, who played admirably under the circumstances. The Packers didn’t pressure him much, presumably preferring to force him to beat them in max coverages, but Capers changed it up with a rare zone blitz that kept the Packers in control. Raji briefly engaged center **Olin Kreutz** before dropping into coverage. Hanie never saw Raji, and the play epitomized Green Bay’s defensive evolution over the last two seasons.

It was a perfect example of why the Packers’ success runs deeper than Rodgers’ right arm, and Green Bay’s defense has been phenomenal for much of the season. During Green Bay’s five-game winning streak — the Packers’ first two victories got them the final seed in the playoffs, and their last three got them into the Super Bowl — the defense has allowed just 14.2 yards per game while forcing 16 turnovers.

Rodgers will have to be better for the Packers to win the Super Bowl, but he certainly won’t have to be perfect. The Packers’ stout defense will have his back, just like they did Sunday in Chicago.

**Jay Christopher Cutler** (born April 29, 1983) is an American former professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") who played in the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) for 12 seasons. A member of the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") for most of his career, he is the franchise leader in passing yards, passing touchdowns, attempts, and completions. Cutler played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Vanderbilt Commodores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_football "Vanderbilt Commodores football"), winning [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference") Offensive Player of the Year in 2005. He was selected by the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") in the first round of the [2006 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NFL_draft "2006 NFL draft"). During his three seasons with the Broncos, he earned [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl") honors in 2008. The following year, Cutler was traded to the Bears, where he played eight seasons. His most successful season was in 2010 when he led the Bears to a division title and [NFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_Championship_Game "NFC Championship Game") appearance. After being released by Chicago, Cutler spent his final season with the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"). He was named among the [100 greatest Bears of All-Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears#Top_100_greatest_Bears_of_all-time "Chicago Bears") in 2019. Cutler was born in [Santa Claus, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Claus,_Indiana "Santa Claus, Indiana"), in 1983. Cutler attended [Heritage Hills High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heritage_Hills_High_School "Heritage Hills High School") in [Lincoln City, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_City,_Indiana "Lincoln City, Indiana").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-3) He [started](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starting_lineup "Starting lineup") three years as a quarterback for the Patriots football team, amassing a combined 26–1 record in his junior and senior years, including a perfect 15–0 during his senior year. Cutler and his team outscored opponents 746–85, including a 90–0 shutout at [Pike Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pike_Central_High_School "Pike Central High School"). During his senior year, Cutler connected on 122 of 202 passes (60.4%) for 2,252 yards with 31 [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown"), while rushing 65 times for 493 yards with 11 touchdowns.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) He also started at [safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_/(American_football_position/) "Safety (American football position)") for three years, [intercepting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interception "Interception") nine passes as a senior, 12th overall in the state.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) His team's perfect record during his senior year included the school's first 3A state championship, where Heritage Hills beat [Zionsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionsville,_Indiana "Zionsville, Indiana") in [overtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_/(sports/) "Overtime (sports)"), 27–24. As an 11-game starter, he completed 273 of 462 passes (59.1%) for 3,073 yards and threw 21 touchdowns and nine interceptions, as he became the first Commodore to win the SEC Offensive Player of the Year (coaches and media) since 1967.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-12) With his senior-season performance, Cutler became the second Commodore to throw for more than 3,000 yards in a season, while his 273 completions and 21 touchdowns ranked second on the school's single-season list.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) He led the Commodores to victories over [Wake Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_football "Wake Forest Demon Deacons football"), [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_Razorbacks_football "Arkansas Razorbacks football"), [Ole Miss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Miss_Rebels_football "Ole Miss Rebels football"), [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Richmond "University of Richmond") and [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Volunteers_football "Tennessee Volunteers football").[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-15)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-16) The Commodores also scored the second most points ever (42) laid upon the [Florida Gators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_football "Florida Gators football") at their current home field at [Ben Hill Griffin Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Hill_Griffin_Stadium "Ben Hill Griffin Stadium"). Vanderbilt nearly upset the 13th-ranked Gators before falling 49–42 in the second overtime after a controversial excessive celebration call prevented the Commodores from going for 2 at the end of regulation.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-17) Reflecting on Cutler's college career, former [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") safety [John Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lynch_/(American_football/) "John Lynch (American football)") said, "If this guy can take a bunch of future doctors and lawyers and have them competing against the Florida Gators, this guy is a stud."[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-18) Cutler ended his career by leading Vanderbilt past [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Volunteers_football "Tennessee Volunteers football"), 28–24, their first over the Volunteers since 1982 (the year before Cutler was born) and the first in [Knoxville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knoxville "Knoxville") since 1975.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-VandySports-19) Cutler passed for three touchdowns and 315 yards, becoming the first quarterback in school history to record four consecutive 300-yard passing performances.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) Cutler's final play in college was the game-winning and streak-ending touchdown pass to teammate [Earl Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Bennett "Earl Bennett") against Tennessee. Cutler was ranked by many experts as the third-best quarterback prospect in the [2006 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NFL_draft "2006 NFL draft") after [Matt Leinart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Leinart "Matt Leinart") of [USC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California") and [Vince Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Young "Vince Young") of [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_at_Austin "University of Texas at Austin"). [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")'s [Chris Mortensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Mortensen "Chris Mortensen") and [Ron Jaworski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Jaworski "Ron Jaworski") tabbed him as the best quarterback available in the draft, and some [scouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scout_/(sport/) "Scout (sport)") believed he had better arm strength than Young and Leinart comparing him to [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") for his [gunslinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunslinger "Gunslinger") attitude.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-29)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-30) At the 2006 [NFL Scouting Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Scouting_Combine "NFL Scouting Combine"), Cutler completed 23 repetitions of a 225-pound [bench press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bench_press "Bench press") (more than some linemen) and ran a [40-yard dash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40-yard_dash "40-yard dash") in 4.77 seconds.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-packers2006-27) Cutler was selected, with the 11th pick of the first round of the draft by the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), who traded their 1st and 3rd round picks to the [St. Louis Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Rams "St. Louis Rams") to move up.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-31) Many believed Cutler was chosen by the Broncos due to the lackluster performance in the previous season's [AFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_playoffs,_2005-06#AFC:_Pittsburgh_Steelers_34,_Denver_Broncos_17 "NFL playoffs, 2005-06") of [Jake Plummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Plummer "Jake Plummer").[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-32) After the pick by Denver, Cutler said, "We had no warning. I think I knew about 15 seconds before everyone else did."[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-33) Cutler, as predicted by most, was the third quarterback chosen, after Young (3rd overall) and Leinart (10th). He is the third first-round pick to come from Vanderbilt, preceded by [Will Wolford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Wolford "Will Wolford") and [Bill Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Wade "Bill Wade"). On July 27, 2006, Cutler agreed to terms on a six-year $48 million contract, which included $11 million in bonuses.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-34) After a strong training camp in 2006, Cutler was promoted from third to second on the Broncos' quarterback [depth chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_chart "Depth chart") ahead of [Bradlee Van Pelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradlee_Van_Pelt "Bradlee Van Pelt"). He passed for more yards than any other rookie in the preseason. On November 27, head coach [Mike Shanahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Shanahan "Mike Shanahan") officially announced that Cutler would replace [Jake Plummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Plummer "Jake Plummer") as starting quarterback despite a 7–4 record because, "I think he gives us the best chance to win now."[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-Post_official-35)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-Broncos_starter-36) The controversial decision capped weeks of speculation and rumors about Cutler's impending promotion to a starting role.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-Tennesseean_Shan-37) Cutler took his first NFL snap on December 3 (Week 13), and, after some initial jitters (0–3 with sack and fumble), completed his first touchdown to [tight end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tight_end "Tight end") [Stephen Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Alexander_/(American_football/) "Stephen Alexander (American football)") in the second quarter.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-38) In the fourth quarter, he threw a memorable 71-yard touchdown to fellow-rookie [Brandon Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Marshall "Brandon Marshall") to tie the game 20–20. It was one of the longest touchdown passes for a debut in NFL history and was also the second-longest pass play between two rookies in Broncos history.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) He also had two interceptions and took three sacks in the loss.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-39) On December 10, in a road loss against the [San Diego Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_San_Diego_Chargers_season "2006 San Diego Chargers season"), Cutler connected with tight end [Tony Scheffler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Scheffler "Tony Scheffler") for two touchdowns in a span of 48 seconds, which is tied for fastest in league history that two rookies produced a pair of scoring passes.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) Cutler's first win came in his third start on December 17, which was a 37–20 road victory over the [Arizona Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Arizona_Cardinals_season "2006 Arizona Cardinals season").[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-40) He finished the game 21-of-31 with 261 yards, two touchdowns, an interception, and a QB rating of 101.7, the highest for a Broncos' rookie since [John Elway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Elway "John Elway") in 1983.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) One touchdown traveled 65 yards in the air, and was recorded as a 54-yard touchdown to [Javon Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javon_Walker "Javon Walker") on the Broncos' third play of the game. Shanahan said to the media, "You saw what he could do today. It doesn't take a genius out there to figure out this guy is very composed, can make all the throws and plays with a lot of confidence."[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-baum_2006_az-41) Cutler then led the Broncos to a [Christmas Eve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Eve "Christmas Eve") win over the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals"), 24–23, in his fourth start on the season.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-42) He went 12-of-23 with 179 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. He also directed the Broncos on a 99-yard drive in the third quarter that culminated on a [Mike Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Bell_/(running_back/) "Mike Bell (running back)") two-yard touchdown run. As a result of the two passing touchdowns in the game against the Bengals, Cutler became the first rookie QB in NFL history to throw for at least two touchdowns in each of his first four games played.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) He also became the second rookie in league history (fifth player overall) to throw at least two touchdown passes in each of his first four starts.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4)[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-rasizer_calm-43) The Broncos' quest to clinch a playoff berth came up short in the final game of the season when they fell at home, 26–23, in overtime to the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers"). The loss dropped the Broncos to 9–7 overall and 4–4 at home. Despite sustaining a concussion in the first half, Cutler finished 21 of 32 with 230 yards and a touchdown and led Denver on a game-tying touchdown drive in the closing minutes of regulation to force overtime.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-44) In five games, Cutler finished with a record of 2–3 and went 81-of-137 for 1,001 yards, nine touchdowns, and five interceptions, earning a franchise rookie record passer rating of 88.5.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-45) He posted the second-highest touchdown percentage (6.6) and third-highest TD-to-INT ratio (1.8) among NFL rookies since 1970 with at least 125 passing attempts.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) [![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Jaycutler.JPG/250px-Jaycutler.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jaycutler.JPG) Cutler preparing for the [Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans") in a 2007 MNF game. The [2007 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NFL_season "2007 NFL season") marked Cutler's first full season as the starting quarterback for the Denver Broncos. In the first game of the season against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills"), Cutler led Denver to a comeback win on a 12-play, 42-yard drive culminating in a [Jason Elam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Elam "Jason Elam") 42-yard [field goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_goal_/(football/) "Field goal (football)") as time expired.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) Cutler's pass attempts (39), completions (23), and yards (304) for the game were career-highs at the time.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) He led Denver to their second straight comeback win the next week in the home opener against the Oakland Raiders. Late in regulation, Cutler moved the team 78 yards in 15 plays for the game-tying field goal with 2:18 remaining.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-broncossitebio-4) The game went into overtime, where he engineered a 52-yard drive that led to another game-winning field goal by Elam. rating").[\[210\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-210) On March 9, 2017, Cutler was released by the Bears through a $2 million [buyout After Cutler's lackluster performances and injuries, the move was expected for months, as the Bears decided to award a $45 million contract to [Mike Glennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Glennon "Mike Glennon").[\[211\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-211) In May 2017, Cutler announced his retirement from professional football and was hired by Fox Sports to be a commentator.[\[212\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-212)[\[213\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-213)[\[214\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-214) On August 3, 2017, [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") quarterback [Ryan Tannehill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Tannehill "Ryan Tannehill") suffered a season-ending injury, and the team reached out to the retired Cutler.[\[215\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-215) On August 7, Cutler signed a one-year, $10 million contract with the Dolphins, reuniting him with former Bears offensive coordinator Adam Gase, who was hired as Miami's head coach in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Miami_Dolphins_season "2016 Miami Dolphins season").[\[216\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-Dolphins-216)[\[217\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-217) In Week 2, the Dolphins won their first game against the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers"), 19–17. Cutler was 24-of-33 for 230 yards with a touchdown to wide receiver [Kenny Stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Stills "Kenny Stills") in the road victory.[\[218\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-218) In a Week 7 game against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_New_York_Jets_season "2017 New York Jets season"), Cutler suffered multiple cracked ribs.[\[219\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-219) He was replaced by [Matt Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Moore_/(American_football/) "Matt Moore (American football)") during the game and was ruled out for the following week's game against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens").[\[220\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-220) He returned in Week 9 to face the [Oakland Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders "Oakland Raiders"). In the 27–24 loss, he was very efficient going 34-of-42 for 311 yards and a touchdown.[\[221\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-221) In the Week 11 game, Cutler suffered a concussion, which caused him to miss the team's next game.[\[222\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-222) Cutler had his best performance of the year in a Monday Night Football game against New England where he outplayed Tom Brady and the Dolphins upset the Patriots. Cutler threw three touchdowns in the win.[\[223\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-223) On December 27, he said he would probably only continue his NFL career if he can be a starter, stating, "I wouldn't want to move again or go somewhere just to back up."[\[224\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-224)[\[225\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-225) He started 14 games and finished with 2,666 passing yards, 19 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions for the Dolphins in the 2017 season.[\[226\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-226) The Dolphins did not make the playoffs and Cutler went 6–8 as a starter. Many teammates, including receiver [Kenny Stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Stills "Kenny Stills"), praised Cutler during the season; Stills described him as "a good man." "People in other places have kind of given him a hard time. I got to know him as a man and as a player and I appreciate him. I like him. "Edit section: Driving while intoxicated conviction")\] On October 17, 2024, Cutler was arrested in [Franklin, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin,_Tennessee "Franklin, Tennessee"), on suspicion of [driving while intoxicated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_under_the_influence "Driving under the influence") and possessing a firearm while under the influence. It was also reported that he attempted to flee the scene and pay the driver of the car he crashed into $2,000 to not call the police, and later refused sobriety testing.[\[266\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-charges-266) He was released from Williamson County Jail after posting a $5,000 bond.[\[267\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-267) Cutler has been charged with DUI-first offense, possession of a handgun-under the influence, failure to exercise due care to avoid a collision and implied consent.[\[266\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler#cite_note-charges-266) On August 26, 2025, Cutler was sentenced to four days in jail as part of a plea deal with prosecutors. As part of the agreement, prosecutors dismissed the weapons possession charge, and Cutler entered a guilty plea to driving under the influence. He was ordered to surrender a pistol found in his car at the time of the accident, pay a $350 fine and attend a DUI safety class, in addition to being placed on unsupervised probation for one year. [Alan Goldsher](https://www.si.com/nfl/bears/onsi/author/alan-go)|

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fnfl%2Fbears%2Fonsi%2Fnews%2Fchicago-bears-in-the-nfc-championship-revisiting-their-last-trip)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Chicago%20Bears%20in%20the%20NFC%20Championship:%20revisiting%20their%20last%20trip&url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fnfl%2Fbears%2Fonsi%2Fnews%2Fchicago-bears-in-the-nfc-championship-revisiting-their-last-trip)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fnfl%2Fbears%2Fonsi%2Fnews%2Fchicago-bears-in-the-nfc-championship-revisiting-their-last-trip&title=Chicago%20Bears%20in%20the%20NFC%20Championship:%20revisiting%20their%20last%20trip)

![Image 2: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Hanie does Caleb Hanie things in the 2010 NFC Championship Game](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_crop,x_0,y_0,w_3858,h_2170/c_fill,w_720,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/images/ImagnImages/mmsport/bear_digest/01jjhg3k36e2xjyc2nae.jpg)

Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Hanie does Caleb Hanie things in the 2010 NFC Championship Game | Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fnfl%2Fbears%2Fonsi%2Fnews%2Fchicago-bears-in-the-nfc-championship-revisiting-their-last-trip)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Chicago%20Bears%20in%20the%20NFC%20Championship:%20revisiting%20their%20last%20trip&url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fnfl%2Fbears%2Fonsi%2Fnews%2Fchicago-bears-in-the-nfc-championship-revisiting-their-last-trip)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fnfl%2Fbears%2Fonsi%2Fnews%2Fchicago-bears-in-the-nfc-championship-revisiting-their-last-trip&title=Chicago%20Bears%20in%20the%20NFC%20Championship:%20revisiting%20their%20last%20trip)

[Add us on ![Image 3: Google Discover](https://assets.minutemediacdn.com/platform/google_discover_icon.svg)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=si.com) 

* * *

In terms of the quarterback position, the Chicago Bears are traditionally, oh, let’s be polite and say _unsettled_.

Since 1985, a whopping 45 Bears have started behind center—an average of 1.125 QBs per season—among them Henry Burris, Moses Moreno, Peter Tom Willis, and Steve Stenstrom.

And let’s not forget Caleb Hanie.

A product of Colorado State and the franchise’s lone quarterback named Caleb aside from our Mr. Williams, Hanie played three seasons for the Bears, his highlight being a mop-up appearance in the 2010 NFC Championship Game at Soldier Field, a January 3, 2011 rumble with Chicago’s eternal rivals, the Green Bay Packers.

Caleb did his best that afternoon. It wasn’t enough.

Smokin’ Jay
-----------

Jay Cutler was the Bears 2010 starter, and—ironically, considering he racked up the most wins in any single season of his career (10)—he was a statistical mess, tossing 16 picks to his 23 touchdowns and taking a career-worst 52 sacks.

But considering Chicago’s solid defense, Cutler didn’t need to be great, as the D allowed just 17.9 points per game, numbers that were good enough to drag the Bears to that aforementioned Packers clash.

Knee Deep
---------

In the third quarter of the Championship game, Cutler sprained his MCL—an injury that had some around the league unfairly [_**questioning his toughness**_](https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcnorth/post/_/id/73789/five-years-ago-jay-cutlers-toughness-was-questioned-in-nfc-title-game)—after which second-string journeyman Todd Collins was sent in to overcome a 14-0 deficit.

Collins stunk up the joint—zero completions on four attempts—so in came Hanie.

To his credit, Hanie played relatively well, putting up 153 yards on 13-of-20 passing, ultimately leading the team to a game-tightening touchdown with four minutes left in the game.

Unfortunately, the touchdown came just one series after he threw a game-losing pick-six to 330-pound tackle B.J. Raji. But still.

No Return
---------

The Bears haven’t seen the NFC Championship Game since 2010’s quarterback snafu—they were close in 2018, then came [_**the Double Doink**_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_Doink)—but hopefully that’ll change as some point (very) soon with the arrival of innovative head coach Ben Johnson.

And hopefully present Caleb will eclipse past Caleb.

Bears–Packers rivalry

The Bears, Lance Briggs (#55) and Brian Urlacher (#54) lining up against the Packers and Aaron Rodgers (#12) in a 2011 game

  • 1941 NFL Western Divisional: Bears won: 33–14
  • 2010 NFC Championship: Packers won: 21–14
The **Bears–Packers rivalry** is a [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) [rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_rivalries "List of NFL rivalries") between the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") and [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-3) The rivalry began in the [1921 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1921_APFA_season "1921 APFA season") when the Packers joined the American Professional Football Association (APFA). Since then, both teams have competed against each other every season, except for the 1922 and 1982 seasons. The Bears and Packers have been rivals in the same conference or division since the NFL adopted its conference structure in [1933 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1933_NFL_season "1933 NFL season"). They were part of the [NFL's Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_and_Western_Conferences_/(NFL/)_1933%E2%80%931969 "Eastern and Western Conferences (NFL) 1933–1969") from 1933 until 1970. Following the [AFL–NFL merger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFL%E2%80%93NFL_merger "AFL–NFL merger"), the Bears and Packers were assigned to the [National Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference") (NFC) and the [NFC Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_Central "NFC Central"), which was later rebranded as the [NFC North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_North "NFC North") during the [2002 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_NFL_season "2002 NFL season"). The Bears maintained a dominant winning record over the Packers for several decades, at two times leading the series by as many as 24 games. However, due to exceptional quarterback performances from the Packers and ongoing struggles and inconsistency from the Bears, the Packers surpassed the Bears in the overall series record during the [2017 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2017 Green Bay Packers season").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-7) They are two of the oldest teams in the NFL. At 212 meetings, it is the league's most-played matchup.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-OnceMore-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-9) Both franchises rank among the top five in the NFL for [all-time win-loss records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_all-time_NFL_win%E2%80%93loss_records "List of all-time NFL win–loss records"), with both holding the record for the most wins in league history. Recently, the Packers overtook the Bears in the [2022 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2022 Green Bay Packers season"), achieving the record for the most overall wins in NFL history. Together, they boast 77 inductees in the Pro Football Hall of Fame (41 from Chicago and 36 from Green Bay) and have collectively secured 22 NFL championships (13 for Green Bay and 9 for Chicago), the highest and second-highest totals in the league. Additionally, they have won five Super Bowl titles, with Green Bay achieving four and Chicago one.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:0-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:1-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:2-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:3-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:4-14)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:5-15)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:6-16)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:7-17) The Packers lead the overall series, 109–97–6. The two teams have met twice in the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_playoffs "National Football League playoffs"), winning one each.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-Head2Head-1) Background ---------- The Bears originated in [1919](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1919_Decatur_Staleys_season "1919 Decatur Staleys season") as the [Decatur Staleys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decatur_Staleys "Decatur Staleys"), a [works team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Works_team "Works team") of the [A. E. Staley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._E._Staley "A. E. Staley") Manufacturing Company. They transitioned to professional status in [1920](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_Decatur_Staleys_season "1920 Decatur Staleys season") and became a charter member of the [American Professional Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Professional_Football_Association "American Professional Football Association") (APFA), which later evolved into the NFL, within the same year. In the [1921 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1921_Chicago_Staleys_season "1921 Chicago Staleys season"), the team relocated to [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") and adopted the name Bears in the [1922 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1922_Chicago_Bears_season "1922 Chicago Bears season"). Similarly, the Packers were established in [1919](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1919_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1919 Green Bay Packers season"), initially supported by the [Indian Packing Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Packing_Company "Indian Packing Company") and later by the Acme Packing Company. They became a member of the APFA in [1921](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1921_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1921 Green Bay Packers season"). Notable games and moments ------------------------- ### 1920s–1950s * **Staleys 20, Packers 0** (November 27, 1921) – The two organizations played for the first time in 1921 at Chicago, when the Bears were named the Chicago Staleys. Bears' [Gaylord "Pete" Stinchcomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaylord_Stinchcomb "Gaylord Stinchcomb") scored the game's first touchdown on a 45-yard run. The Bears shut out the Packers 20–0 in their first meeting, and the rivalry was born. A year later, the Staleys changed their team name to the Bears. * **Bears 3, Packers 0** (November 23, 1924) – The Bears–Packers rivalry can be credited for the first ever ejection of players for fighting during an NFL game. The Bears' [Frank Hanny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Hanny "Frank Hanny") and Packers' [Tillie Voss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tillie_Voss "Tillie Voss") were ejected before the end of the first half as verbal exchanges led to punches being thrown. Two years later, Hanny was ejected once again in a game versus Green Bay. * **Packers 7, Bears 0** (September 28, 1930) – The Packers shut out the Bears for the fifth consecutive game in this contest which is the longest such streak in the series. The streak began in 1928 when the Packers defeated the Bears 6–0 on December 9 of [that season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1928 Green Bay Packers season").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1928_Green_Bay_Packers-18) In [1929](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1929_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1929 Green Bay Packers season"), the Packers shut out the Bears three times, 23–0, 14–0, and 25–0 en route to their first [NFL championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1929_NFL_season "1929 NFL season").[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1929_Green_Bay_Packers-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1929_NFL_Standings-20) On November 9, the Bears finally scored on the Packers although they came up short in the final score 13–12.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1930_Green_Bay_Packers-21) The Packers then went on to win their second consecutive [NFL title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_NFL_season "1930 NFL season") that season.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1930_NFL_Standings-22) * **Packers 7, Bears 0** (September 22, 1935) – On the first play of the game, rookie receiver [Don Hutson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Hutson "Don Hutson") scored on an 83-yard touchdown pass from [Arnie Herber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnie_Herber "Arnie Herber") for the only score of the game. This was Hutson's first career reception and touchdown in what would become a historic Hall of Fame career.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-23) * **Bears 30, Packers 3** (September 20, 1936) – During a dominant Bears victory, Packers fan Emmett Platten, out of frustration, ran out onto the field and punched Bears lineman [Ted Rosequist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Rosequist "Ted Rosequist"), believing Rosequist had committed several dirty plays on the Packers. Rosequist was knocked out by the punch and had to be removed from the game.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-24) Platten received no actual punishment for his actions, but was publicly admonished by the _Green Bay Press Gazette_ newspaper. * **Packers 16, Bears 14** (November 2, 1941) – The Bears came into the game undefeated and seemingly invincible. Over their first five games, they defeated their rivals by an unprecedented 157 points.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1st_Five_Games-25) However, the Packers upset them in this game which was the Bears lone defeat that season. The Associated Press wrote of the game that the "Chicago Bears myth is broken".[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-Myth_is_Broken-26) Chicago fans made accusations that the game had been fixed, and it was suggested that the Packers had employed a "secret" defensive scheme. The Packers had built a 16–0 lead through the first three quarters of play before the Bears mounted a comeback in the fourth quarter coming up just short of a win.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-Packers_16_at_Bears_14-27) * **Bears 33, Packers 14** (December 14, 1941) – In the first playoff meeting between the two rivals, the Bears defeated the Packers 33–14 in a one-game-playoff to determine the Western Division championship. After the Packers, the Bears defeated the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1941_New_York_Giants_season "1941 New York Giants season") en route to their fourth [NFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1941_NFL_Championship_Game "1941 NFL Championship Game"). Until the 2010 post-season, this remained the only playoff meeting between the teams. * **Bears 52, Packers 31** (November 6, 1955) – The Bears and Packers played the highest-scoring game of their series at Soldier Field in the 1955 season. The Bears created a huge 45–3 lead, but the Packers were able to score 28 points in the fourth quarter; by the game's end, the Bears beat the Packers 52–31, with the two teams combining for 83 points. This was also the last game that [George Halas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Halas "George Halas") coached the Bears in against the Packers until 1958 due to a temporary break from coaching. * **Packers 21, Bears 17** (September 29, 1957) – The Packers hosted the Bears in the inaugural game of their brand new stadium, initially called New City Stadium (later changed to [Lambeau Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field") in 1965). Among the attendees to the game included NFL Commissioner [Bert Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bert_Bell "Bert Bell"), United States Vice President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon"), actor [James Arness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Arness "James Arness"), and Miss America 1958, [Marilyn Van Derbur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Van_Derbur "Marilyn Van Derbur"). Playing behind several times during the game, the Packers finally were able to gain the lead in the 4th quarter on a 6-yard touchdown pass from [Babe Parilli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babe_Parilli "Babe Parilli") to [Gary Knafelc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Knafelc "Gary Knafelc") for the winning points. * **Packers 9, Bears 6** (September 27, 1959) – In the debut game of new Packers head coach, [Vince Lombardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Lombardi "Vince Lombardi"), the Packers fell behind the Bears 6–0, until [Jim Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Taylor_/(fullback/) "Jim Taylor (fullback)") scored on a 5-yard touchdown run, giving the Packers the lead. [Dave Hanner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Hanner "Dave Hanner") followed the touchdown with a safety, sacking Bears quarterback Ed Brown in the Bears' endzone to cap off the victory. The Packers celebrated their first win under their new coach by carrying him off at the end of the game. ### 1960s–1970s * **Packers 31, Bears 28** (November 12, 1961) – The Packers built up an impressive 31–7 lead in the game, but the Bears made a furious comeback with three unanswered touchdowns to make the score 31–28. Still, the Packers were able to win the game; they would go on to win the [NFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_NFL_Championship_Game "1961 NFL Championship Game") that year against the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_New_York_Giants "1961 New York Giants"). * **Packers 49, Bears 0** (September 30, 1962) – [Vince Lombardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Lombardi "Vince Lombardi")'s Packers shutout [George Halas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Halas "George Halas")' Bears, 49–0 at [City Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field"), the Packers largest margin of victory in the rivalry. The team repeated that score against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_Philadelphia_Eagles "1962 Philadelphia Eagles") six weeks later on Nov 11, 1962. The games remain a Packers team record for most points in a shutout victory. After again defeating the Bears later in the season, this time by a score of 38–7, the Packers won their 8th [NFL championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_NFL_Championship_Game "1962 NFL Championship Game"). Motivated by the two humiliating losses to the Packers, Halas spent the off-season focusing on beating the Packers. * **Bears 26, Packers 7** (November 17, 1963) – The Bears and Packers, both with 8–1 records, met at Wrigley Field to play for first place in the Western Conference. Chicago, behind a dominant defense, got a 26–0 lead and held on to win 26–7, completing a sweep of the Packers in the [1963 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_NFL_season "1963 NFL season") and handling Green Bay only two losses of the season. The Bears finished the season with an [NFL championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_NFL_Championship_Game "1963 NFL Championship Game") victory over the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_New_York_Giants_season "1963 New York Giants season") once again, claiming their 8th NFL Championship. * **Packers 23, Bears 12** (September 13, 1964) – Remembered as the "Free Kick Game" because the Packers invoked the surprising "[Fair catch kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_catch_kick "Fair catch kick") rule", which allows for a place or drop kick field goal attempt from the spot of a fair catch. Packers' coach Vince Lombardi opted to attempt a free kick. Confusion ensued as neither team had ever so much as even practiced a free kick. The Packers lined up at the line of scrimmage with [Bart Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Starr "Bart Starr") holding for [Paul Hornung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Hornung "Paul Hornung"). Hornung made the 52-yard field goal as the first half ended. The Packers stunned all in attendance with the kick and won the game 23–12. * **Bears 13, Packers 10** (November 3, 1968) – The Bears got their revenge on the Packers, beating them 13–10 on a fair catch free kick by [Mac Percival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Percival "Mac Percival") at the 43-yard line after a Packers punt with 26 seconds left in the game. Percival kicked a game-winner the week before against the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings").[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-28)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-29) ### 1980s [![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Steve_McMichael_September_2016.jpg/250px-Steve_McMichael_September_2016.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Steve_McMichael_September_2016.jpg) [Steve McMichael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_McMichael "Steve McMichael"), a Hall-of-Famer, spent most of his career with the Chicago Bears before concluding his time in the NFL with the [1994 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1994 Green Bay Packers season") with the Green Bay Packers. * **Packers 12, Bears 6** (September 7, 1980) – With the score tied 6–6 and the game in overtime, Packers kicker [Chester Marcol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_Marcol "Chester Marcol") was called in to attempt a game-winning field goal. Two years later, [Bill Tobin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Tobin_/(American_football/) "Bill Tobin (American football)"), the Bears' vice president of player personnel at the time, revealed that he had been instructed by general manager Jim Finks during the off-season to study film and decode the Packers' signal system for relaying plays to the quarterback. "I went at it like a tiger does good meat," Tobin said at the time. * **Bears 23, Packers 7** (October 21, 1985) – The world was introduced to rookie defensive lineman [William "The Refrigerator" Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Perry_/(American_football/) "William Perry (American football)") on [Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday_Night_Football "Monday Night Football").[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-AmericasGame-32) In goal line situations, Bears head coach [Mike Ditka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ditka "Mike Ditka") used Perry, who weighed roughly 300 lbs in the fullback position. Packers cornerback [Mark Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Lee_/(American_football/) "Mark Lee (American football)") was ejected after he and Bears running back Walter Payton went flying over a bench in the first quarter.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1985_Chicago_Bears_vs_Green_Bay_Packers-33) A few minutes later, Packers safety [Ken Stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Stills "Ken Stills") was flagged for hitting [Matt Suhey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Suhey "Matt Suhey") of the Bears well after the whistle. The very next month, the Bears would release their song [The Super Bowl Shuffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Super_Bowl_Shuffle "The Super Bowl Shuffle") (two months before they won the Super Bowl), making them the only team of any professional sport to record a US Hot 100 hit and receive a Grammy nomination. * **Bears 12, Packers 10** (November 23, 1986) – In Week 12 of the 1986 season Green Bay defensive tackle [Charles Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Martin_/(football_player/) "Charles Martin (football player)") wore a towel with a hit list of specific Bears numbers written on it, such as No. 34 Walter Payton, No. 9 [Jim McMahon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_McMahon "Jim McMahon"), and others.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-34) Following a McMahon interception Martin came up from behind and body slammed him to the turf purposely well after the whistle[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-1985_Chicago_Bears_vs_Green_Bay_Packers-33) separating McMahon's shoulder and ending the quarterback's season. Martin was suspended for two games, at the time the longest suspension in NFL history.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-35) * **Packers 14, Bears 13** (November 6, 1989) – This became known as the [Instant Replay Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instant_Replay_Game "Instant Replay Game").[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-IR_Bears_MG-36) Packers quarterback [Don Majkowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Majkowski "Don Majkowski") led the Packers to a comeback with an apparent game-winning touchdown pass to wide receiver [Sterling Sharpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_Sharpe "Sterling Sharpe"). This led to a change in the "illegal forward pass" rule which defined when to consider a passer past the line of scrimmage.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-ZEBRA-37) The rule used to be judged by the position of the ball instead of the passer's feet. Bears coach Mike Ditka ordered that an asterisk be placed next to the result in all team publications. ### 1990s * **Packers 33, Bears 6** (October 31, 1994) – Playing with a severely bruised hip in a driving rainstorm at [Soldier Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldier_Field "Soldier Field") on Halloween Night, [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") rushes for a career-high 58 yards – including a 36-yard touchdown in the second quarter when he leaped over a Bears defender.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-Brett_Favre_memorable_moments-38) After the game Favre said "Maybe [Gale Sayers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gale_Sayers "Gale Sayers") (who had his number retired that night along with [Dick Butkus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Butkus "Dick Butkus")) got excited about that one".[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-Chicago_very_owned-39) With a win in that game, Green Bay began a ten-game winning streak against the Bears as Favre was considered a "Bear-killer". Late in the second quarter, defensive lineman [Roy Robertson-Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Robertson-Harris "Roy Robertson-Harris") knocked Aaron Rodgers out with a knee injury and the Bears capitalized with Mack getting a pick-six off Packers backup [DeShone Kizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeShone_Kizer "DeShone Kizer"). Rodgers would return to the game in third quarter down 20–0, and led the Packers on a scoring drive culminating in a [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") field goal to end the third quarter with the Bears leading 20–3. However, the Packers outscored the Bears 21–3 off three Rodgers touchdown passes, to take a 24–23 lead with just over 2 minutes left. The Packers would hang on to win by that score. The 17-point fourth-quarter comeback for the Packers represented their largest in franchise history. However, the teams would head in opposite directions going forward. * **Bears 24, Packers 17** (December 16, 2018) – Following their Week 1 meeting, the Bears and Packers had gone in opposite directions during the 2018 season. The 5-7-1 Packers and 9-4 Bears met in Soldier Field for a Week 15 showdown with major implications in the playoff race for both teams. The Bears needed a win to clinch the NFC North, while a Packers victory would keep their slim playoff hopes alive. Led by a dominant defensive performance and two touchdown passes from Mitchell Trubisky, the Bears would win the game 24-17 (their first win over the Packers at Soldier Field since [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Chicago_Bears_season "2010 Chicago Bears season")) and clinched the NFC North while eliminating the Packers from playoff contention. Linebacker [Khalil Mack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalil_Mack "Khalil Mack") would sack Aaron Rodgers 2.5 times while safety [Eddie Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Jackson_/(safety/) "Eddie Jackson (safety)") intercepted Rodgers late in the fourth quarter to seal the Bears victory (and also breaking Rodgers' NFL-record streak of 402 consecutive passes without an interception). The Packers would finish the season 6-9-1 (their first time since 1990–91 with back-to-back losing seasons) while the Bears would finish 12–4, losing in the Wild Card round to the [Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Philadelphia_Eagles_season "2018 Philadelphia Eagles season") in the [Double Doink Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_Doink_Game "Double Doink Game"). * **Packers 10, Bears 3** (September 5, 2019) – 2019 was the NFL's [100th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NFL_season "2019 NFL season"). It was also the Chicago Bears' [100th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Chicago_Bears_season "2019 Chicago Bears season") in the NFL. The NFL decided to pay tribute by deciding the match up of the [first game of their season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Kickoff_Game "NFL Kickoff Game") on Thursday with the NFL's longest rivalry, the Packers and the Bears at Soldier Field.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bears%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-53) The decision would break the NFL's yearly tradition of their first game being the defending Super Bowl champions at their home field which would've been the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") at [Gillette Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gillette_Stadium "Gillette Stadium") since the Patriots won [Super Bowl LIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIII "Super Bowl LIII") the previous year. The Bears' only points in the game would be a field goal in the 1st quarter while the Packers scored a touchdown in the 2nd quarter and a field goal in the fourth quarter as the Packers won the game 10–3. The game was officially sealed when two newly signed Packers free agents, safety [Adrian Amos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_Amos "Adrian Amos") (who was previously on the Bears) and linebacker [Preston Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_Smith_/(linebacker/) "Preston Smith (linebacker)") made plays that ended the Bears' final two offensive drives. * **Packers 21, Bears 13** (December 15, 2019) – The Bears and Packers would meet at Lambeau Field in a Week 15 matchup that, like the 2018 matchup, would have major playoff implications for both teams. The Packers needed a win to keep their hopes for an NFC North title alive, while the Bears needed a win plus a [Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Minnesota_Vikings_season "2019 Minnesota Vikings season") loss to stay alive in the playoff hunt. After the Packers raced to a 21–3 lead in the third quarter, the Bears would score 10 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to cut the lead to 21–13. It took until the game's final play to seal the game, as the final play of the game was a botched lateral by the Bears that was recovered by the Packers' [Tramon Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramon_Williams "Tramon Williams"). In a role reversal of 2018, the Packers eliminated the Bears from playoff contention with the win and clinched the NFC North a week later with a Monday Night win at the Vikings. The Packers would finish the season 13–3, falling to the [49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_San_Francisco_49ers_season "2019 San Francisco 49ers season") in the [NFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NFC_Championship_Game "2019 NFC Championship Game"), while the Bears finished the season 8–8. ### 2020s * **Packers 35, Bears 16** (January 3, 2021) – The
